title: Sitting with breathlessness, panic, or faster breathing near the end

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: Breathing looks fast, laboured, or frightening; the room becomes alarmed, and the family needs a way to witness breathlessness without inventing treatment or timing from it.
ordinary_language_queries: breathless dying person what to do
fast breathing end of life panic
looks like he cannot breathe dying

content_layers.observation_text: NICE includes assessment and management of breathlessness in the last days of life, including reversible causes, non-pharmacological options, medication review, and specialist advice when needed.
content_layers.source_synthesis: The record is intentionally professional-source-weighted because breathlessness can be distressing and treatment-sensitive. It can orient a witness, but must not instruct them how to medicate or oxygenate.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: Breathlessness is one of the places where the corpus must be most useful and most restrained: the witness needs language immediately, but the archive cannot become the clinician.

what_this_is_not: not opioid, benzodiazepine, or fan advice for a particular person
not proof of pain, panic, or time remaining
uncertainties: Breathlessness may have reversible or treatable contributors.
Urgency depends on the care plan and setting.
Future witness records should separate what the room saw from what the person later reported, if known.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should validate that frightening breathing deserves care-team contact when worried, while avoiding unsupported reassurance or treatment steps.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect language for explaining breathlessness, visible distress, oxygen debates, medication boundaries, and how to tell families when to call.
language_notes: Keep “air hunger” as a term but define cautiously.
Avoid “just part of dying” when the reader is worried.
Do not minimize distress because a source says a symptom can be common.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
